subject: Business
title: Mobile Money: Banking the Unbanked
description: One-minute skill: Mobile Money: Banking the Unbanked.

hook.text: In Kenya, a farmer pays for seeds with a text message. No bank, no card, just a phone.

buildup.text: M-Pesa launched in 2007, letting Kenyans send money via basic mobile phones. No smartphone needed.

discovery.text: Within a decade, M-Pesa processed more transactions than Western Union did globally.

twist.text: Mobile money leapfrogged traditional banking entirely. Countries that lacked banks now lead in digital finance.

climax.text: Today, over 1.75 billion mobile money accounts exist worldwide, mostly in developing nations.

punchline.text: The future of money was built in Africa, not Silicon Valley.

quiz.question: What made M-Pesa revolutionary?
options: It allowed money transfers via basic mobile phones without a bank account
It was the first cryptocurrency in Africa
It used facial recognition for payments

details.summary: Mobile money services like M-Pesa in Kenya allow people without bank accounts to send, receive, and store money using basic mobile phones. Launched in 2007, M-Pesa brought millions of unbanked Africans into the financial system through simple SMS-based transactions.
details.whyItMatters: M-Pesa proved that banking does not require banks. Mobile money has lifted millions out of poverty by providing access to savings, credit, and payments, demonstrating that financial inclusion transforms economies from the bottom up.
takeaways: M-Pesa enables financial transactions using basic mobile phones via SMS
Over 50 million people in Kenya use mobile money services regularly
Mobile money reduced extreme poverty in Kenya by an estimated 2 percent

faq.question: How does M-Pesa work without a bank account or smartphone?
faq.answer: Users register with an ID and get a mobile money account linked to their phone number. They deposit and withdraw cash through a network of agents in shops and kiosks. Transfers and payments happen via simple text messages on any basic mobile phone.

faq.question: Why did mobile money succeed in Africa but not in the United States?
faq.answer: Most Americans already had bank accounts and credit cards, so mobile money solved a problem that did not exist. In Kenya, over 80 percent of adults were unbanked when M-Pesa launched, creating massive unmet demand for basic financial services that the system addressed.
